subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add `openclaw models status --probe --all` as the canonical configured-model health check now, or fold this behavior into broader fallback-chain or staged-migration diagnostics?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the command makes real provider calls and overlaps other model-diagnostic feature requests, so automation should not choose the permanent product contract alone.

options.title: Add Focused Status Probe
options.body: Implement `models status --probe --all` as an additive, opt-in live probe mode over configured primary, fallback, image, and image-fallback model refs, preserving existing `--probe` behavior by default.

options.title: Fold Into Fallback/Migration UX
options.body: Make the fallback-chain or staged model-migration work own configured-model validation and keep status probes limited to auth/provider diagnostics.

options.title: Defer New Live Probe Surface
options.body: Leave current auth probes as-is until maintainers define a broader provider diagnostics and support-policy roadmap.

recommendation.title: Add Focused Status Probe
recommendation.body: Implement `models status --probe --all` as an additive, opt-in live probe mode over configured primary, fallback, image, and image-fallback model refs, preserving existing `--probe` behavior by default.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current live models status auth probes and has the strongest combined history across the CLI/status/probe files that would define the product contract.
